summary: CCC-built 1937 fire tower (also ET-12) on Holston River Mountain in Bays Mountain Park, Kingsport area; NHLR-registered 2020. Height sources conflict (60 vs 100 ft).

facts.design: CCC-built fire tower with a seven-foot-square lookout shelter at the top (1953 description)

staffing.status: seasonal lookout, about five months a year (1953 Times-News)

access.note: NHLR lists the location as Bays Mountain Park; the history site places the tower on the Holston River Mountain ridge that borders the park. Visit Kingsport advertised a ranger-guided hike that goes up inside the tower. General opening rules were not confirmed.

visit.trail_note: 3.3 miles round trip; the last 8 tenths of a mile is steep with steps and switchbacks; not ADA compliant (Visit Kingsport)

corrections.proposed: unresolved: 30.5 (100 ft, per NHLR and Bays Mountain history) or 18.3 (60 ft, per 1953 Times-News)
corrections.why: The brief's 18.0 m (60 ft) comes only from the 1953 newspaper. The NHLR page and the Bays Mountain history site both say 100 feet. The sources conflict, so the value should be marked unresolved until checked.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR and Bays Mountain history say 100 feet; the 1953 Times-News says 60 feet. The story reports both and no single height fact is recorded.
Bays Mountain history says the tower stands on Holston River Mountain, which borders Bays Mountain Park. The 1953 Times-News says atop Bays Mountain. The story gives both.
NHLR gives 2,393 ft (729 m); the regional table gives 2405 ft. The story gives both.

notes_for_editor: Build year and CCC attribution agree across NHLR and the Bays Mountain history site. The height conflict is unresolved; no third source was read. The 1953 article gives the lookout's details (five months a year, cabin, phone and weather checks). Forestry service use into the 1960s comes from the Bays Mountain history site only, so no end year is recorded. Visit Kingsport describes a guided early-arrival hike, which is not proof of general public access, so the access level is public with a note. The brief's elevation 729.4 m matches the NHLR 729 m figure. A search also turned up an Appvoices hiking article (2018) that credits the CCC; it was not read and is not cited. The Kingsport Times-News article is cited through the Bays Mountain history reproduction. Verification 2026-10-08: the story's 'within Bays Mountain Park' claim was changed to the NHLR location field, because the history site says the tower stands on the ridge that borders the park; the cabin is now described as where nights were spent, not as built 'for him'.
